data.name: Fractile Raises $720M at $7B Valuation for AI Inference Chips
data.summary: UK startup Fractile, founded in 2022 by Walter Goodwin, secured $720 million in Series C funding led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed, and Redpoint, with backing from the UK government and investors like BlackRock. The company builds custom chips that integrate DRAM directly onto logic for faster AI inference, tackling memory limits in long-context tasks like agentic AI. Goodwin plans to ship the world's fastest inference chips next year, targeting data centers in 2027, amid surging demand for efficient hardware beyond Nvidia.
data.hook: Fractile's founders are stacking memory right on top of their processors to smash AI bottlenecks. This massive funding round shows big belief in their bold hardware bet.

data.summary: The San Francisco startup emerged from stealth with a $47 million seed round led by 8VC and Fundomo to develop AI-powered instruments for endovascular surgery. These tools capture real-time data from blood vessels, creating 3D maps that guide catheters precisely and make expert procedures more accessible. Pirozzi and Mackanic, Stanford PhD alumni, aim to scale rare surgical skills to help more patients with life-saving care. The company is now hiring in San Francisco to advance sensing, perception, and robotics.

data.name: Index Industries Launches Tokenized U.S. Home Price Index with $50M Seed
data.summary: Index Industries emerged from stealth with a $50 million seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, announcing USHP—a tokenized index that tracks U.S. home prices for liquid, onchain investing. data.name: Meta Launches Muse Ember, Its Smallest Most Efficient AI Model
data.summary: Released on November 9, Muse Ember excels at repetitive jobs such as tool calls, routing, and long document handling, scoring 36 on the Intelligence Index—matching rivals like Claude Haiku 5.5—at about a third the cost or less. It features a 1-million-token context window, supports text, images, audio, and video, and runs on Meta's API, Muse Code, and Google Cloud. Early tests show it whipping up dozens of websites and animations in minutes for pennies, making high-volume AI work affordable for developers everywhere.
data.hook: Meta just unveiled Muse Ember, a tiny AI powerhouse designed for the endless grind of agent tasks like coding and document parsing. Executives call it a game-changer for smarts per dollar.

data.name: Tendrils Compute Raises $30M to Redesign CPU from Scratch
data.summary: Tendrils Compute, a UK startup, secured $30 million led by Benchmark, with Jack Altman joining the board to support their bold plan for a general-purpose processor featuring thousands of parallel cores based on interaction nets. The chip aims for better scalability, locality, and energy efficiency, paired with their open-source programming language Vine. Backers like the UK Sovereign AI fund and tech voices praise the ambition, as AI's growing needs highlight flaws in traditional multi-core CPUs. Founder Cremer's vision has drawn strong support, signaling hope for a hardware breakthrough.

data.name: Gakku.ai Raises $51M for AI Coach That Teaches Kids Through Conversation
data.summary: Gakku.ai just raised $51 million to build Raku, an AI coach for kids ages 6 to 16 that focuses on writing, speaking, and critical thinking via voice chats and lesson maps. Instead of handing out answers, Raku interviews users, pushes back on ideas, and encourages them to explain and express themselves. Co-founder Annie Chen stresses that in the AI era, helping kids articulate their thoughts builds deeper understanding and self-awareness. Parents and experts praise it for keeping children actively engaged, with one dad noting it suits his young son's love for drawing over rote schoolwork.

data.name: Lila Sciences Unveils Open-Ended AI Research Breakthroughs
data.summary: Lila Sciences released a vision blog and four preprints from its Open-Endedness team, led by Kenneth Stanley, challenging ideas like whether more data always improves AI or if rewarding creativity directly sparks the best results. Key work introduces UFOs, a technique for unified factored representations that create sharper, more stable networks, as shown in a skull image comparison where Picbreeder-style training beats blurry standard results. The papers also tackle the 'creative paradox' and training LLMs to stay naïve for fresh perspectives, with researchers praising the potential for better coding agents and tying into the company's AI Science Factories.

data.name: Vangrid Raises $9M to Power Robotics with Crowdsourced Phone Mapping
data.summary: Vangrid secured $9 million in seed funding from backers like HashKey Capital and Animoca Brands to build a crowdsourced mapping system using everyday phones. Contributors capture spots like pedestrian crossings for bounties, with data blurred for privacy, fingerprinted on the Base blockchain, and turned into 3D models for robotics and Physical AI. The network has logged over 1.25 million captures from hundreds of thousands of users, settling more than $600,000 in USDC, tackling the need for fresh spatial data that robots can't get from the internet. CEO Robert Brighton calls it the decentralized perception grid to keep billion-dollar robots from going blind in dynamic environments.
data.hook: Imagine turning your smartphone into the eyes for robots navigating real streets. Dutch startup Vangrid is making that happen with a decentralized network already live and buzzing.
